enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B: PROBLEM SOLVING**

**4.** *Study the passage and answer the questions that follow:*

> Every parent is a counsellor. My father being one, once told me, "hard work is like a cup of milk and luck is like a spoon of sugar". Since the Bible, one of the oldest books of our time declares that God always gives sugar to those who have a cup of milk, these words of wisdom must be unquestionably true. Either I have a cup of milk or God will not give me sugar. Since that day, I resolved to know a good thing when I see one and I don't let it slip away. If I get a chance, I take it and if it changes my life, I let it. But experience shows that life is both good and bad at the same time.

**Questions**
incertitudes: Q4(a)(i) : le passage contient une contradiction explicite (« life is both good and bad at the same time ») : loi de non-contradiction retenue. Texte du passage recopié tel qu'imprimé.

Q4(b)(ii) : deux formes hypothétiques équivalentes sont possibles (« If I do not have a cup of milk, then God will not give me sugar » et sa contraposée) ; la première est retenue, la seconde donnée en équivalent.
Q4(e)(i) : la conclusion d'un dilemme constructif complexe est la disjonction des conséquents (« Either I take it or I let it »).
Q4(e)(ii) : plusieurs étiquettes sont défendables (appel à l'autorité, appel à l'ancienneté / à la tradition) ; appel à l'autorité (ad verecundiam) retenu.

Règle de choix : la page de garde dit « answer FIVE questions, taking ALL the THREE Questions from Section A and ANY TWO from Section B ; only the first five questions answered will be marked ». Section A (questions 1 à 3) : toutes obligatoires, donc aucune règle ; Section B (questions 4 à 6) : `parmi 2 sur 3`. La règle « les cinq premières réponses seules sont corrigées » est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`.
Points : chaque question est imprimée « 20 marks ». Chaque sous-question (a) à (e) vaut 4 points (2 x 2) ; Q2(a) est imprimée « 4x1 marks ». 5 x 4 = 20 : aucun écart de somme.

Aucun corrigé officiel ; les corrigés sont des réponses modèles de manuel de logique traditionnelle (définitions, règles de distribution, carré des oppositions avec import existentiel). Les tables de vérité, la validité du dilemme constructif complexe et des syllogismes (AEE-2, AAA-1, EAE-1) sont recalculées avec Python. questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) (i) Which Law of Thought is violated in the passage above?

(ii) Pick out a universal Term from the passage. (2x2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** The **Law of Non-Contradiction**. The passage ends with "life is both good and bad at the same time": the same thing is said to have a quality (good) and its opposite (bad) at the same time and in the same respect, which the law forbids (nothing can be both A and not-A at the same time and in the same respect).

**(ii)** **"Every parent"** (the term "parent"): it is quantified by "every", so it refers to all members of the class and is a universal term.
themes: O Level Logic - laws of thought
O Level Logic - definition and division

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) (i) Identify a Disjunctive Proposition in the passage.

(ii) Translate the Proposition in b(i) above into a Hypothetical Proposition. (2x2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** **"Either I have a cup of milk or God will not give me sugar."** (p = I have a cup of milk; q = God will not give me sugar; form: p v q.)

**(ii)** "Either p or q" is equivalent to "if not p, then q". So: **"If I do not have a cup of milk, then God will not give me sugar."** (Equivalent form: "If God gives me sugar, then I have a cup of milk.") A truth-table check confirms that p v q, ~p then q and ~q then p have the same truth-values in all four rows.
themes: O Level Logic - propositions and their types

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) Using the variables p and q, symbolise this statement: "God gives you sugar if and only if you have a cup of tea".

(ii) Determine the Truth-Value of the symbolized statement in c(i) above given that p is True and q is False. (2x2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** Let p = "God gives you sugar" and q = "You have a cup of tea". "If and only if" is the biconditional (equivalence): **$p \equiv q$**.

**(ii)** A biconditional is true only when both sides have the same truth-value.

| p | q | $p \equiv q$ |
|---|---|---|
| T | T | T |
| **T** | **F** | **F** |
| F | T | F |
| F | F | T |

With p True and q False the statement is **False**.
themes: O Level Logic - symbolic logic basics

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) (i) Using "every parent is a counsellor" as the given, infer its Contrary.

(ii) Determine the Major and Minor Terms in the following Syllogism:

"All hardworking persons are successful in life

No lazy persons are successful in life

Therefore, no lazy persons are hardworking persons" (2x2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** "Every parent is a counsellor" is an **A** proposition. Its contrary is the **E** proposition with the same subject and predicate: **"No parent is a counsellor."** (Contraries cannot both be true; they can both be false.)

**(ii)** The conclusion is "No lazy persons are hardworking persons".
- **Minor term** (subject of the conclusion): **lazy persons**.
- **Major term** (predicate of the conclusion): **hardworking persons**.
- (Middle term: successful in life.)

The major term appears in the first premise and the minor term in the second, as it should. The syllogism is A E E in the second figure, which is valid.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(e) (i) Draw a Conclusion from the following Premises to produce a Complex Constructive Dilemma:

"If I get a chance, I take it and if it changes my life, I let it.

Either I get a chance or it changes my life".

(ii) Identify the Fallacy most clearly committed in this Argument: "Since the Bible, one of the oldest books of our time declares that God always gives sugar to those who have a cup of milk, these words of wisdom must be unquestionably true". (2x2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** The first premise holds two conditionals: (A then B) and (C then D), with A = I get a chance, B = I take it, C = it changes my life, D = I let it. The second premise affirms the antecedents: A or C. A complex constructive dilemma concludes the disjunction of the consequents:

**Therefore, either I take it or I let it** (B v D).

It is "complex" because the two consequents are different, and "constructive" because the antecedents are affirmed. A truth-table check over all 16 combinations confirms the form is valid.

**(ii)** **Appeal to authority (argumentum ad verecundiam).** The claim is held to be "unquestionably true" only because an old and respected book says so, not because of evidence for it. The age of the book (appeal to antiquity) is irrelevant to the truth of the claim. It is a fallacy of relevance.
